Customs

Thông quan nhập khẩu

The formal process by which imported goods are authorized for entry into a country after compliance with all customs requirements, payment of duties, and submission of necessary documentation.

Quick answer: The formal process by which imported goods are authorized for entry into a country after compliance with all customs requirements, payment of duties, and submission of necessary documentation.

Quick answer

The formal process by which imported goods are authorized for entry into a country after compliance with all customs requirements, payment of duties, and submission of necessary documentation.

Why it matters

Thông quan nhập khẩu matters because it supports clear communication in Customs contexts for Freight Forwarders, Supply Chain Managers, and Customs Brokers. It also connects to aviation training and exam language such as FIATA Diploma, CILT Certification, and IATA DGR.

Questions and answers

What is Thông quan nhập khẩu?

In this glossary, Thông quan nhập khẩu refers to: The formal process by which imported goods are authorized for entry into a country after compliance with all customs requirements, payment of duties, and submission of necessary documentation.

How is Thông quan nhập khẩu used in logistics?

In logistics communication, this term appears in contexts such as: "Cần hoàn thành thủ tục thông quan nhập khẩu trước khi hàng được giao cho người nhận tại cảng nhập."

Why does Thông quan nhập khẩu matter in logistics?

Thông quan nhập khẩu matters because it supports clear communication in Customs contexts for Freight Forwarders, Supply Chain Managers, and Customs Brokers. It also connects to aviation training and exam language such as FIATA Diploma, CILT Certification, and IATA DGR.

Where does this definition come from?

This definition is sourced from Incoterms 2020 (ICC), FIATA, IATA DGR, WCO and published by Protermify Logistics as a static logistics reference page.

Definition

The formal process by which imported goods are authorized for entry into a country after compliance with all customs requirements, payment of duties, and submission of necessary documentation.

Operational example

Import clearance is required before goods can be delivered to the consignee from the port of entry.
